definitions.gloss: oblong; landscape-oriented; horizontally long; wider than tall
definitions.explanation: Describes a shape or object that is wider than it is tall — the horizontal dimension is longer than the vertical. Used for objects, screens, paper orientation, and architectural features.

examples.japanese: {横長|よこなが}の{封筒|ふうとう}を{使|つか}う。
{横長|よこなが}の{画面|がめん}で{動画|どうが}を{見|み}る。
examples.english: To watch videos on a wide screen.

examples.japanese: リビングに{横長|よこなが}の{大|おお}きなソファを{置|お}いたら、{部屋|へや}がずいぶん{狭|せま}くなった。
examples.english: When I put a long, wide sofa in the living room, the room became quite cramped.

notes:
Describes something wider than it is tall. Composed of {横|よこ} (horizontal/side) + {長|なが} (long). Can be used as a noun or as a no-adjective modifier ({横長|よこなが}の).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {横長|よこなが}の{封筒|ふうとう}: landscape envelope
- {横長|よこなが}の{画面|がめん}: widescreen
- {横長|よこなが}の{建物|たてもの}: horizontally elongated building
- {横長|よこなが}のテーブル: oblong table

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {縦長|たてなが}: portrait-oriented; taller than wide — the opposite of {横長|よこなが}
- {細長|ほそなが}い: long and thin — emphasizes thinness rather than horizontal orientation

USAGE:
In digital contexts, {横長|よこなが} corresponds to "landscape orientation" (as opposed to {縦長|たてなが} for "portrait orientation"). In everyday use, it describes any object, shape, or space that extends more horizontally than vertically.
